title: A protocol for reconstructing the dynamics of real-world systems from observational data: Application for establishing a digital proxy of a bioreactor (DIYBOT)
protocol: Collect continuous sensor data at 15-minute intervals for a 60-day period.
Transition the bioreactor to steady state operation over the first 40 days, characterized by less than 5% deviation in treatment and dampened oscillatory behavior.
Add a pulse of 1.0 mg/L AgNP on day 40.
Incrementally add pulses of AgNP at subsequent 30-day intervals (2.0 mg/L on day 70; 3.0 mg/L on day 100).
Store time series data each week and back up on an external hard drive for subsequent processing.
Use R version 3.6.1 and the forecast v8.12 package to conduct Fourier spectrum analysis.
Conduct singular spectrum analysis using the Rssa 0.13-1 package.
Utilize tseriesChaos package for further data analysis as needed.
Signal process the three AgNP pulses for the O₂ and pH records as described.
Perform Fourier frequency spectrum analysis on the raw data.
Plot the raw O₂ data with a 15-minute time scale.
Plot the raw pH data with a 60-second time scale.
Generate Fourier spectra using the forecast v8.12 package.
Plot the generated Fourier spectra.
Remove the mean and divide by the standard deviation for each sensor time series to standardize the data.
Rerun the Fourier Spectrum on the resampled 2-hour blocks to ensure that it reproduces the dominant 50-hour oscillation in 25 two-hour blocks.
Compare empirical attractor characteristics to corresponding surrogate attractor characteristics.
Test the null hypothesis that there is no significant difference in the measured characteristics.
Prepare summary tables of surrogate data testing for rapid analysis.
Compute the maximum Lyapunov Exponents from the empirical and phenomenological attractors.
Use numerical partial derivatives computed from the phenomenological models to measure the marginal response of a response variable to an incremental change in a driving variable.
Quantify interactions detected with CCM using numerical partial derivatives.
Observe that when AgNP concentrations are at or below 2.0 mg/L, pH has a negative marginal impact on O₂.
Note that when AgNP concentration is 3.0 mg/L, pH has a detrimental impact on O₂ and this relationship decays over time.
Determine that positive values of the curve indicate a positive marginal impact between variables.
Identify that negative values of the curve indicate a negative marginal impact between variables.
Recognize that if the curve decays to zero, it indicates that over time the impact decays (is non-persistent).
